entries.german:
Karl IV. verfügt, daß das vom früheren Olmützer Bischof Johann dem Nonnenkloster Ad misericordiam dei in Prag Benediktinerordens geschenkte Haus in der grossern Stadt Prag nach dem Tode des Bischofs Theodorich von Minden und des Prager Bürgers Heinrich Faist von Regensburg, denen es auf Lebensdauer überlassen ist, den Verträgen gemäß an das Kloster und nicht etwa an den Fiskus fallen soll, da der Bischof von Minden, licet notorie administracioni et dispensacioni rerum et pecuniarum nostrarum presideat easdemque ad nutum nostre maiestatis tam generaliter dispenset quam legaliter administret, die großartigen, am Hause vorgenommenen Bauten nicht aus dem Ärar sondern aus den ihm vom Kaiser für seine unzähligen Dienste verliehenen Geldern und Einkünften bestritten hat.

Zeugen: venerabiles Arnestus Pragensis archiepiscopus, Johannes Olomucensis, Johannes Luthomuschlensis, imperialis aule cancellarius, et Maurus Corbaviensis ecclesiarum episcopi, illustres Rydakarus Brunswicensis, Bolko Swidnicensis, Bolko Opuliensis et Przimyslaus Teschinensis duces, spectabilis Ulricus comes de Helfenstein, Johannes burgravius Magdeburgensis, nobiles Jesco et Wanko de Wartemberg, Jodocus, Ulricus et Johannes fratres de Rosemberg, Swinko de Hasemburg, Hasko de Swereticz et Busko de Wilharticz, magistri camere imperialis, et alii quamplures nostri et imperii sacri principes, nobiles et fideles.
entries.english:
Karl IV decrees that the house in the larger town of Prague, which the former Bishop Johann of Olomouc gave to the Benedictine nunnery Ad misericordiam dei in Prague and which was granted for life to the Bishop Theodorich of Minden and the Prague burgher Heinrich Faist of Regensburg, shall, after their deaths and in accordance with the agreements, pass to the monastery and not to the fisc. This is because the Bishop of Minden, although he notoriously presides over the administration and disposal of our property and money and manages it generally at the will of our majesty as well as lawfully, paid for the great works carried out on the house not from the treasury but from the monies and revenues granted him by the Emperor for his innumerable services.

Witnesses: the venerable Arnest, Archbishop of Prague; Johannes Olomucensis, Johannes Luthomuschlensis, chancellor of the imperial court, and Maurus Corbaviensis, bishops; the illustrious Rydakar, Duke of Brunswick, Bolko, Duke of Schweidnitz, Bolko, Duke of Opole, and Przimyslaus, Duke of Teschen; the distinguished Ulrich, Count von Helfenstein; Johannes, Burgrave of Magdeburg; the nobles Jesco and Wanko von Wartenberg; Jodocus, Ulrich, and Johannes, brothers von Rosenberg; Swinko von Hasenburg, Hasko von Swereticz, and Busko von Wilharticz, masters of the imperial chamber; and many other princes, nobles, and faithful men of ours and of the Holy Empire.
